newsitem.title: India: TEXT - Chidambaram's reply to debate on India budget.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - Chidambaram's reply to debate on India budget.

text.p: (The following is the text of Indian Finance Minister P.Chidambaram's address in the parliament on Friday in reply to a debate on the federal budget for 1996/97).

The capital market is a place where almost 20 million Indians have invested their hard earned savings. The shareholding population in our country is growing rapidly as families seek new and productive outlets of increasing the value of their savings.
Indian companies and entrepreneurs are raising increasing amounts of money from the capital market to start new factories, launch new businesses and expand existing enterprises.

The capital market goes up and down. While speculation is an unavoidable feature of any market, we must impart a certain stability to our markets so that the interests of millions of small investors are protected. We have already empowered SEBI.
I am determined to move against errant brokers and merchant bankers and dishonest promoters. Some action has already been taken. But more can be done and will be done.

In the past several weeks, I have been inundated with requests from various sections of society that I should do something to revive the capital markets which have been going through a sluggish phase for quite some time.

The state of the markets has to be constantly under review and watch. There are no one-time or magic solutions. The Indian capital market suffers from a number of structural weaknesses which I intend to address systematically.
But I am persuaded that there is urgent need to perk up market sentiment since a good part of market behaviour is based on psychology and sentiment.
Accordingly, I am happy to announce the following measures:

* Under Section 54 EA of the Income Tax Act which I have proposed in the Finance Bill under consideration, capital gains exemption is to be given if the investment is made for three years in bonds or debentures notified by the CBDT, I propose to expand the coverage to include investment in all mutual funds.

* Under Section 54 EB of the Income Tax Act which I have proposed in the Finance Bill under consideration, capital gains is to be exempted from tax if the gains are invested in specified assets notified by the CBDT and retained for seven years. I intend to include debentures and units of all mutual funds in "specified assets".

* Under Section 80 L of the Income Tax Act, the exemption limit in respect of income by way of dividend and interest from certain specified investments in securities is 13,000 rupees. Some years ago, this limit was divided into two parts.

I propose to revert to a two-part arrangement. I propose to raise the exemption limit to 15,000 rupees but divide it into two parts of 12,000 rupees and 3,000 rupees. 3,000 rupees will be exclusively reserved for income from investment in shares and mutual funds. UTI should be happy; so will other mutual funds.

* Individuals, Indian companies and foreign companies pay capital gains at the rate of 20 percent. Honourable Members will recall that in order to create a level-playing field I made this an uniform rate in my Budget speech.

However, partnership firms alone are required to pay at the rate of 30 percent. In order to remove the discrimination, I am reducing the capital gains of partnership firms from the existing 30 percent to 20 percent.

* Some stock exchanges have set up investor protection funds. It is good to have such funds and encourage the growth of such funds. I therefore propose to exempt all such funds from income tax provided the net income from such funds is ploughed back into the corpus. A suitable provision will be made in the Income Tax Act in due course.

* Honourable Members will be pleased to learn that the RBI is separately announcing an increase in the existing limit for bank advances to individual against security of shares and debentures from 0.5 million rupees to 1 million rupees.

* I would like to see a greater degree of corporatisation of the Indian broker community. It is in the national interest to have more corporates as brokers and to encourage more brokers to become corporates.
Such corporate brokers will be subject to the discipline of the company law. We would also be able to enforce capital adequacy and other norms.

I intend to invite shortly leading stockbrokers, both individuals and firms, to a discussion to consider a scheme to facilitate the conversion of brokers into public limited companies. I look forward to a positive response and a fruitful dialogue.

* I am convinced that we must have large institutions as major buyers in the stock market. Until new institutional players emerge, UTI and LIC will have to share a big responsibility. These institutions are being strengthened and will be professionalised so as to make them effective and responsive participants in the equity market. I will ask the boards of LIC and UTI to take steps towards these goals.

* In my budget speech, I had announced the increase in the limit of investment for each FII in a company from 5 percent to 10 percent. In respect of debt instruments, FIIs are allowed to invest upto 30 percent of their total funds. There are several FIIs that manage or intend to manage dedicated debt funds. It has been decided to allow FIIs to invest upto 100 percent of their funds in debt instruments. Details will be announced by SEBI in due course.
